rule: Loose shapes are slid toward the jagged wall band and stacked so each piece interlocks exactly into the wall's notches and into the previous piece, forming a solid column against the wall.
gap: Needs jigsaw-style fitting: choose order and offset so pieces interlock with wall gaps and each other, not just move-until-contact.

rule: The grid contains a main fragment and a detached fragment, each marked with 7 cells; the detached fragment is moved and overlaid so its 7-marked cells coincide with the main fragment's 7s, gluing the drawing together and cropping to the union (7s become 4).
gap: Needs splitting grid into fragments and aligning them via marker-anchor correspondence (offset search), then union-crop; overlay only supports equal-size separator panels.

rule: Each small shape left of the frame is moved into the frame, centred at every intersection of a row and column whose border marker cells (left and top frame edges) have the shape's colour; shapes without matching markers stay put.
gap: Border cells act as coordinate pointers: needs binding shape colour to row/column markers and copying the shape to each marked intersection.

rule: Coloured blocks lie in 2-row strips on an 8 background; the 1/2 border lines give the reading orientation, and the blocks are read strip by strip in that order, rotated upright, centred to the widest block's width and stacked vertically.
gap: Needs extracting a sequence of sub-objects, ordering them by marker-given reading direction, and re-assembling them centred in a stacked output.

rule: Irregular hand-drawn nested closed loops and dots are redrawn as a clean schematic: each loop becomes a 1-cell-spaced rectangle, preserving the containment tree and left/right arrangement of inner shapes and dots.
gap: Needs topology-preserving abstraction of irregular curves (containment tree) and re-rendering as canonical nested rectangles; no shape normalisation exists.

rule: Colour-6 streams flow downward from the top; when a stream hits a horizontal 2-bar it wraps the bar with a 6 outline (row above and both sides) and continues falling from both ends, recursively, until the bottom.
gap: Rays stop or pass obstacles but cannot split and flow around them; needs a recursive water-flow behaviour with outlining and branching.

rule: A legend row lists colours in sequence; for each consecutive pair (a,b) the box with centre a is joined to the adjacent box with centre b by a bridge in colour a, tracing a path through the boxes in legend order.
gap: Connect only joins same-colour cells; needs reading an ordered colour sequence legend and drawing bridges between boxes in that order.

rule: Border 2-markers define cut lines across the grid (drawn in 2, with 7 where the line crosses the object); the 7 shape is cut along these lines and each piece slides to the grid corner/edge in its own quadrant, keeping its shape.
gap: Needs cutting one object by marker-defined lines and moving each sub-part independently to its region's corner; moves act on whole objects only.

rule: Several fragments are scattered on the background; fragments whose edge columns/rows are identical overlap there, and they are chained together edge-to-edge (rotating where needed) into one assembled object which is output cropped.
gap: Needs matching fragment boundaries and searching the chaining order/orientation to assemble one object; no edge-matching or multi-part assembly exists.

rule: The black panel lists colours in a column; output is that panel with each colour's row extended to show one dot (spaced by 1) per object of that colour found in the rest of the grid.
gap: Needs counting objects per colour outside the panel and rendering counts as dot rows inside the cropped legend panel.

rule: Each object slides vertically to the grid edge: objects whose cell count equals that of another object move to the top edge, objects with a unique cell count move to the bottom edge (column kept).
gap: Gravity direction must be conditioned on a relational property (size shared with another object); move/gravity uses one fixed direction per task.

rule: Each black shape slides right until it touches the vertical 5 line; then every row in which the shape encloses a closed background hole gets its cells right of the 5 line painted 2.
gap: Requires chaining move-until-contact with a row-wise marking conditioned on enclosed holes in the moved shape; modules apply one rule each.

rule: The first panel contains a dividing line that splits it into two regions; the empty fourth panel is filled with panel 2's pattern on one side of that line (including the line) and panel 3's pattern on the other side.
gap: Panel vote/overlay is cellwise boolean; needs a region mask derived from a line in one panel to select between two other panels per region.

rule: Four irregular pieces are rotated/reflected and packed together without gaps into a solid square whose area equals their total cell count, with the piece carrying the 5 cell placed so the 5 lands at the top-left corner.
gap: Needs a polyomino packing search over D8 poses and positions of several pieces into a square; composition only selects or overlays.

rule: Each shape touching a colour-2 marker is copied as its mirror image across that marker: a 2-line acts as a reflection axis, a single 2 cell as a point of 180-degree rotation.
gap: Symmetry axis must be per-object, anchored on the attached 2 marker (line axis or point centre), rather than a global grid axis.

rule: A wiggly path anchored at one end to a straight bar is swung over to the other side, re-drawn as a curve that hugs the third (target) object while keeping its length and anchor point; the original path is erased.
gap: Needs non-rigid re-shaping of a path to wrap around a target object while preserving anchor and length; no deformable path model.

rule: Closed loops are linked by thin paths into networks; a corner marker cell (e.g. 4/7, or 6/8 in test) sits at the end of a network, and every loop connected to that marker's network has its interior filled with the marker colour; other loops stay empty.
gap: Enclosed-fill exists, but must be conditioned on graph connectivity of the loop to a marker via paths, taking fill colour from that marker.

rule: Flood the background region reachable from the 6 seed; cells of that region adjacent (incl. diagonally) to a 1 wall or the grid border become 7, and 1-objects not touching that region are erased.
gap: Needs seeded flood-fill of a region, outlining its boundary, and deleting objects not adjacent to it; fill only handles enclosed background.

rule: Coloured bars on the bottom row act as commands for the column of plus-shapes above them: a 2-bar recolours its column's shapes to 5, and a 3-bar stacks that many extra copies on top of its column as the number of shapes recoloured.
gap: Bar colours encode actions (recolour vs replicate) and the replication count comes from counting shapes in other columns; no action-glyph binding or counting.

rule: A side panel holds a small tile, a mask glyph and indicator boxes (4 and 7 positions in 6-frames) that set orientation/flip; the main canvas is cropped and the tile is stamped repeatedly over the region selected by the scaled-up mask, in the indicated orientation.
gap: Indicator glyphs encode tile orientation and a mask glyph encodes where (scaled) to tile; needs binding these legend parts and composing tile-under-mask.

rule: Every 1-object gets a 2-coloured outline (8-neighbour halo); objects that contain enclosed holes are additionally recoloured 8 with their hole cells set to 6, while hole-free objects stay 1.
gap: Needs a shape-agnostic rule: halo all objects plus recolour-if-holed with hole fill; change tables keyed by exact canonical shape do not generalise to new shapes.

rule: Framed 5x5 boxes slide horizontally: boxes with an 8 frame slide left and boxes with a 2 frame slide right, each stopping at the grid edge or against a previously stopped box.
gap: Gravity direction must be chosen per object by its frame colour, with boxes stacking against each other; dynamics uses one direction per task.

rule: Output is the bounding box of the monochrome mask shape scaled by the multicolour tile's size: each mask cell is replaced by a copy of the tile and each non-mask cell by background.
gap: Fractal/tile exists but only self-similar; needs Kronecker product of one object's mask with a different (multicolour) object as tile.

rule: Shapes carry colour-2 connector dots; keeping the 4 block fixed, all other shapes are translated so that their connector dots coincide pairwise with those of already-placed shapes, assembling one connected structure.
gap: Needs connector-matching assembly: search translations of many pieces so 2-dot pairs coincide, building a tree from the anchor piece.

rule: The small 8 cross (four arms around an empty centre) is the seed of a four-armed rotating spiral: each arm keeps extending and turning in the same rotational direction with 1-cell gaps, filling the whole grid; the seed itself is erased.
gap: Needs a turtle-like spiral-growth behaviour (extend, turn, keep gap) iterated to the grid border from each arm; rays are straight only.

rule: Two noisy solid colour regions: stray pixels outside the regions are deleted, and each background hole inside a region becomes an 8 surrounded by a 3x3 ring painted in the other region's colour.
gap: Needs noise-robust region segmentation plus a hole stamp whose colour is borrowed from the other region; chaining denoise and stamp is unsupported.

rule: Several parallel line segments (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) share a start baseline; each is trimmed or extended along its direction to the length of the median/reference line.
gap: Needs comparing line lengths across objects (median/reference) and extending or trimming each line, incl. diagonals, to that length.

rule: The 3x3 motif in the 6x6 input is colour-inverted (shape->0, background->7) and tiled with period 3 (offset 1) into a fixed 16x16 grid; inside the central 6x6 square the 0 cells become 9.
gap: Tiling exists, but needs motif extraction with colour inversion, phase-shifted tiling to a fixed non-multiple output size, and a constant central overlay chained together.

rule: Amid border noise, a picture sits in the corner formed by two solid single-colour lines; the picture inside that L-frame (lines excluded) is cropped and rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise (then flipped as needed).
gap: Object select + D8 exists, but needs segmenting the picture bounded by touching frame lines amid noise, excluding the frame, before crop-and-rotate.
